q.t: Who was the first Indian to see the Earth from space?
q.e: Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma — he said India looked 'Saare Jahaan Se Achcha'.

q.t: Who was the first Indian to reach the International Space Station?
q.e: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla.

q.t: The Earth looks blue from space because…
o: About three-quarters of it is water
q.e: Most of its surface is ocean.

q.t: From space, can you see country borders?
q.e: Borders are agreements on maps, not physical lines.

q.t: DIGIPIN gives each place a…
q.e: It helps postmen and ambulances find you fast.

q.t: Chilli first came to India from…
q.e: Portuguese travellers brought it 400–500 years ago.

q.t: Marigold came to India from…
q.e: It became part of Indian temples, weddings and Diwali.

q.t: Yoga travelled from…
q.e: Practised in India for over 3,000 years, now almost everywhere.

q.t: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam means…
q.e: All people, animals, plants, rivers and the air belong to one family.

q.t: Rosy starlings fly to India in…
q.e: They come from Russia and Mongolia every winter.

q.t: Why do borders vanish when seen from space?
q.e: A border is an agreement between people, drawn on a map.

q.t: Why does a written address end in 'Earth'?
o: It is the largest true box in a set of nested boxes
q.e: Every address is nested boxes, and the biggest is shared by everyone.

q.t: Why is a code like DIGIPIN better than 'behind the big neem tree'?
o: A code identifies a place and can't be misread
q.e: A description can be misread; a code cannot.

q.t: Why does the rosy starling migrate?
o: No single place suits it all year
q.e: Its northern home is great in summer and lethal in winter.

q.t: How does the rosy starling help Indian farmers?
q.e: A bird that spends half its life in Mongolia protects an Indian crop.

q.t: Before chilli, Indian food was made hot with…
q.e: Pepper is genuinely Indian and was called 'black gold'.

q.t: Why did chilli take over so fast in India?
o: It grew easily, was cheaper than pepper and gave more heat
q.e: Traditions absorb what suits them.

q.t: What did India give the world about sugar?
o: The method of making jaggery and sugar from sugarcane
q.e: Before that, the world sweetened food with honey.

q.t: Which Indian cattle breeds supply most of Brazil's milk?
q.e: More than three-quarters of Brazil's milk comes from them.

q.t: India gave the world the idea of…
q.e: India gave zero and received the potato and chilli.

q.t: 'Nature has no boundaries' means problems like smoke…
o: Cross borders, so countries must work together
q.e: No country can clean its own air alone.

q.t: Why did Indian cows succeed so well in Brazil?
o: They were already bred for heat, humidity and insects
q.e: An animal suited to one place thrives in another with the same conditions.

q.t: Indian cows might fail in a very cold country because…
o: They are adapted to hot, humid conditions
q.e: Adaptation fits a place; different conditions can make it fail.

q.t: Why did both Mexico and India choose marigolds for festivals?
o: Bright, cheap, easy to grow and long-lasting
q.e: When distant peoples pick the same thing, the reasons are usually practical.

q.t: Migration is…
o: A solution to a problem staying still can't solve
q.e: The same route is flown generation after generation.

q.t: What does the chilli story teach?
o: What feels most 'ours' may have arrived recently
q.e: Traditions are not frozen — they absorb.

q.t: Why is the 'world is one family' idea earned by this chapter?
o: It showed evidence first — birds, plants, ideas and cows travelling
It is an old saying only
q.e: The evidence came first and the saying came last.

q.t: A river polluted upstream in one state arrives dirty in another. This shows…
o: Each state has its own river
q.e: Nature has no boundaries.

q.t: Earth is special because…
o: It is the only planet we know with life
It is closest to the Sun
q.e: For thousands of years it has supported life.

q.t: The Ministry of Environment logo reminds us that…
o: Caring for nature is caring for ourselves
q.e: It shows the balance between nature and human life.

q.t: Which is the best way to care for the Earth?
o: Pick one thing you'll really do every day
Make a long list nobody keeps
q.e: One well-chosen daily habit beats a long ignored list.

q.t: Which travelled India → Brazil deliberately?
q.e: Portuguese traders took Indian cattle to Brazil.

q.t: Which travelled South America → India?
q.e: Chilli arrived 400–500 years ago.

q.t: Which shows 'ideas travel'?
q.e: Yoga was carried by travellers, scholars and teachers.

q.t: Nobody's kitchen is 'entirely home-grown' because…
o: Every culture includes things from elsewhere
q.e: Every culture is partly made of things that came from somewhere else.

q.t: An astronaut sees land masses and seas but not your village. Why?
o: It is far too small from that height
q.e: From space you see only broad shapes.

q.t: Which pair is matched correctly?
q.e: Sugar-making knowledge spread from India.

q.t: Why must almost every country talk to every other about the environment?
o: No country can solve it alone
q.e: Both problems and solutions cross borders.

q.t: 'Saare Jahaan Se Achcha' was said by…
q.e: He said it when asked how India looked from space.

q.t: If you list where things in your house first came from, you'll find…
q.e: Clothes, food, games and trees often came from far away.
